newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Union to hold mass action day in SAfrican province.
newsitem.headline: Union to hold mass action day in SAfrican province.

text.p: South Africa's largest labour union the Congress of South African Trade Unions (Cosatu) on Thursday said its organisation in the province of Mpumalanga would hold a day of marches to protest about employment legislation.
Cosatu threatened in February to hold a general strike on May 12 in support of its demands on negotiations for an Employment Bill.
Among Cosatu's conditions are a 40 hour working week, six months maternity leave with four months paid and Sunday work to be paid at double wages.
Cosatu said the Mpumalanga marches would be held on Friday at Secunda, Nelspruit and Witbank.
"Mass action is now needed to shift the balance of power in favour of workers and to a more worker friendly Employment Law," Cosatu said.
